label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
statement_en: Whatever the law of increase in a linear dimension, volume and therefore weight tend to vary as the cube of linear dimensions, which mainly (though not wholly) explains why the human weight curve differs in shape from the stature curve.

length_ratio_vs_reference.note: an implied exponent is ln(X/X_ref) / ln(L/L_ref) against the single reference specimen (Cypselurus hiraii, Park and Choi 2010 Table 1 model L3, SL 0.203 m), so the denominator approaches zero as L approaches L_ref and ordinary specimen variation is amplified without limit. About 1% relative uncertainty in L against the studio's 0.1 decision band means the comparison carries no information until |ln(L/L_ref)| >= 0.1, i.e. a length ratio outside [0.905, 1.105]. lean.source:
/-- **The log-log exponent of a cube law is exactly 3.** -/
theorem cubeLaw_loglog_exponent {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L₁ L₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂) : logSlope W L₁ L₂ = 3 := by
  have hlog : log L₂ - log L₁ ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    exact hne (log_injOn_pos h₂ h₁ (sub_eq_zero.mp h0)).symm
  unfold logSlope
  rw [div_eq_iff hlog, h.2 L₁ h₁, h.2 L₂ h₂, log_mul h.1.ne' (pow_ne_zero 3 h₂.ne'),
    log_mul h.1.ne' (pow_ne_zero 3 h₁.ne'), log_pow, log_pow]
  push_cast
  ring

named_hypotheses.name: Delphi.CubeLaw
named_hypotheses.source:
/-- Isometric growth at constant density: weight is `k` times the cube of the linear dimension. -/
def CubeLaw (W : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℝ) : Prop := 0 < k ∧ ∀ L, 0 < L → W L = k * L ^ 3

constraint_details.canEliminate: the mass side of Galileo's square-cube argument only: a giant with unchanged proportions and density must weigh (L2/L1)^3 times more. Strength scaling as L^2 is NOT formalised, so a candidate claiming the giant can support itself is not ruled out by this theorem
constraint_details.lemma_source:
/-- **C7, interval form.** Weight ratio confined to `[a, b]` and length ratio to `[c, d]` with `0 ≤ c`:
ruled out when `[a, b]` and `[c^3, d^3]` are disjoint. -/
theorem cubeLaw_rules_out' {W : ℝ → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : CubeLaw W k) {L₁ L₂ a b c d : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁)
    (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hr : a ≤ W L₂ / W L₁ ∧ W L₂ / W L₁ ≤ b) (hℓ : c ≤ L₂ / L₁ ∧ L₂ / L₁ ≤ d)
    (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hne : b < c ^ 3 ∨ d ^ 3 < a) : False := by
  have hq := cubeLaw_ratio h h₁ h₂
  have hℓ0 : 0 ≤ L₂ / L₁ := le_trans hc hℓ.1
  have hlo : c ^ 3 ≤ (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3 := pow_le_pow_left₀ hc hℓ.1 3
  have hhi : (L₂ / L₁) ^ 3 ≤ d ^ 3 := pow_le_pow_left₀ hℓ0 hℓ.2 3
  rcases hne with hne | hne <;> linarith [hr.1, hr.2]

constraint_details.canEliminate: a candidate that asserts isometry and a measured exponent whose interval excludes 3 (for example every NHANES window in the claims thread's test, if read as isometric)
constraint_details.lemma_source:
/-- **C7b, the exponent form.** A log-log exponent confined to an interval not containing `3`, under
isometric scaling at constant density, is ruled out for every `k`. -/
theorem exponent_rules_out {W : ℝ → ℝ} {L₁ L₂ a b : ℝ} (h₁ : 0 < L₁) (h₂ : 0 < L₂) (hne : L₁ ≠ L₂)
    (hb : a ≤ logSlope W L₁ L₂ ∧ logSlope W L₁ L₂ ≤ b) (h : b < 3 ∨ 3 < a) : ∀ k, ¬ CubeLaw W k := by
  intro k hk
  have := cubeLaw_loglog_exponent hk h₁ h₂ hne
  rcases h with h | h <;> linarith [hb.1, hb.2]
